purpose: Teach: フラメンコ/イケメン/ハングル/ヒップ/ヒーリング/ショパン/アキバ/レッズ

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんがフラメンコの映像を見せて下さるそうよ
lines.en: Sho, your dad is going to show you a flamenco video.
lines.style: Warm, matter-of-fact announcement. Light lift on 'Dad.' Gentle pace, like sharing a small gift she knows he'll enjoy. Steady, present.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんがイケメンだって言われたよ
lines.en: Mom, someone told me Dad is handsome.
lines.style: Quiet pride mixed with slight shyness. Small, genuine smile in the voice. The careful way a six-year-old shares something he's noticed matters. Soft at the edges.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんがハングルの絵本をお買いになったわ
lines.en: Sho, your dad bought a picture book in Korean.
lines.style: Observant, slightly amused tone. Not quite explaining — just noticing aloud the particular things Dad does. Warm, unrushed.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんとヒップホップ踊ったよ
lines.en: Mom, I danced hip-hop with Dad.
lines.style: Bright, unselfconscious energy. The small joy of a child reporting something he did. Quick cadence, natural enthusiasm without performing.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんがヒーリング音楽を流して下さるそうよ
lines.en: Sho, your dad is going to play some healing music for you.
lines.style: Gently knowing tone — she's watched this pattern before. Affectionate observation, not explanation. Soft and steady, like she's smiling at him.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんとショパンの曲を聴いたよ
lines.en: Mom, I listened to Chopin with Dad.
lines.style: Simple, earnest delivery. The pride of sharing something he's learned. Quiet wonder underneath. No rush to the words.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんがアキバに連れて行って下さるそうよ
lines.en: Sho, your dad is going to take you to Akiba.
lines.style: Settled, affectionate tone. Announcing the plan like she's been storing up something she knows will make him happy. Warm, patient.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんとレッズの試合観たいよ
lines.en: Mom, I want to watch a Reds game with Dad.
lines.style: Tentative wish-making. Quiet longing in the voice — not demanding, but hoping. The careful tone a child uses when asking for something that matters to him.
